newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says not dumping wheat, rejects export cap.
newsitem.headline: Canada says not dumping wheat, rejects export cap.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Lyle Vanclief, reacting to remarks by top U.S. officials, said on Thursday that Canada was not dumping wheat and had no interest in reinstating a cap on its wheat exports.
"We are fair traders and play by the rules," he told Reuters after the remarks in Washington by U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman and U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky.

"We are certainly not interested in capping the amount of trade. We're not asking the Americans or Mr. Glickman to cap the amount of wheat that the Americans are exporting into Canada this year, which is incredibly higher than it has been in many, many years," Vanclief said.

He said he did not know what Barshefsky meant in describing U.S. exports to Canada as "quite limited." They were nearly four times as high as last year and last year was considerably higher than it had been in many years, he said.

Glickman said, after meeting with senators from northern U.S. states, that the U.S. administration was very concerned about Canadian exports. Barshefsky said the Commerce Department might investigate whether Canada was dumping its wheat -- selling it unfairly cheaply -- in the United States.
"Three investigations have proven before that we're not doing that. We're not doing anything different than before, so there's no cause for anyone to even use the word dumping," he said.

The United States has often expressed concern with the fact that the government-supervised Canadian Wheat Board runs a wheat export monopoly, but Vanclief said: "That's been investigated three times, and it's been proven we're not dumping in the United States. We're supplying a market."

He said he had urged Glickman in a conversation a few weeks ago to use the established process of talks between officials of the two neighbors' trade departments to discuss such issues. The last such meeting was on June 27.
"I'm encouraging him to continue the use of that process," he said, adding he had no plans at present to call either Glickman or Barshefsky on their latest remarks.
